observations: Photo 0: white console seen from above, 'Xbox' logo printed top right of the lid, rear half of the lid covered in a round-hole perforated vent grille; a black Xbox wireless controller rests on it; a box marked HDMI at the right edge.
Photo 1: front edge of the console showing a horizontal disc slot and a small button on the right, controller in front; the console is powered off; shop watermark 'Williams Gadgets' over the photo.
Photo 2: front right corner with the Xbox logo power button and the perforated side vents; surfaces look clean with no visible cracks or scratches.
The shape, white finish, perforated grille and front disc slot match an Xbox One S with a disc drive, not a Series S and not the all-digital edition.
No storage size is readable in any photo; no label underneath, no rear ports, no power cable, no screen showing the console running, no receipt.

identity.kind: game console with disc drive and one wireless controller
read_from: photo 0 Xbox logo on the lid
photos 0 to 2 One S body shape, perforated grille and disc slot in photo 1

claims.evidence: Xbox One S is supported by the logo in photo 0 and the body design in photos 0 to 2; the 1TB size is not shown on any label or screen.
One black Xbox wireless controller is visible in photos 0, 1 and 2.
No screen showing the game library.
Top and front look clean in photos 0 to 2, but underside, back, ports and controller wear are not shown.
Internal history cannot be seen from photos; casing seams and screws are not shown.
Console is off in every photo; no clip of it booting or playing.
No receipt or warranty card is shown.

risks.proof: Screenshot or photo of the TV showing Settings > System > Storage, or the label on the underside.

risks.risk: Console does not power on, overheats, or the disc drive does not read discs.
risks.proof: Clip powering on to the dashboard, inserting a disc that loads, and playing a game for a minute.

risks.risk: Controller has stick drift or dead buttons.
risks.proof: Clip of the controller test or a game showing sticks centred and every button responding.
risks.if_unproven: priced as console without a working controller

risks.risk: Console is banned from Xbox Live or still tied to another account.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the console signed into Xbox network showing online status, then reset to factory.

risks.risk: HDMI port, USB ports or power cable missing or damaged.
risks.proof: Photo of the rear ports and of the power and HDMI cables included.

risks.risk: Installed games are only tied to the seller's account and leave with it.
risks.proof: Screenshot of the game library listing which titles are on disc versus digital.

proof_requests: Clip of the console powering on to the dashboard and loading a disc game
Screenshot of Settings > System > Storage showing capacity
Photo of the underside label and rear ports
Clip testing every controller button and both sticks
Photo of the cables and the receipt if available
response.reason: The Xbox logo and the distinctive One S body with disc slot identify the console, so it can be priced at its worst case as a 500GB unit not proven working until a power-on clip and storage screen are shown.
